newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Bank Hapoalim profit up 46 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Bank Hapoalim profit up 46 pct.

text.p: Net profit at Bank Hapoalim, Israel's largest bank, rose 46 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to 316 million shekels from 216 million a year earlier, the company said on Thursday.
Hapoalim attributed the rise to higher profits from financing activities, a reduced provision for doubtful debts and growth in the profits of affiliated companies.
Net return on equity on an annualised basis was 16.6 percent, up from 11.9 percent in the first quarter of 1996.
Profit from financing activities before the provision for doubtful debts rose to 913 million shekels in the first three months of 1997 from 831 million a year earlier.
This resulted in part from a rise in bond prices and from the expansion of off-balance sheet activities, especially forward transactions and financial instruments.
The provision for doubtful debts fell 39.1 percent to 149 million shekels, mostly due to the agricultural sector.

Operating and other income rose to 587 million shekels from 585 million a year earlier. Income from capital market activities rose 1.4 percent in the first quarter after declining in the past two years.
Hapoalim's share in the profits of unconsolidated subsidiary and affiliated companies rose to 98 million shekels from 73 million a year earlier.

The bank's consolidated assets fell slightly to 148.8 million shekels in the first quarter from 149.4 million at the end of 1996. The bank attributed the decline to new reporting procedures regarding financial instruments.
Shareholders' equity rose 4.2 percent from the end of 1996 to 8.4 billion shekels in the first quarter.
Credit to the public rose 1.6 percent from the end of 1996 to 85.7 billion shekels while deposits from the public fell 1.5 percent to 106.9 billion.

Assets controlled by the bank's mutual funds in the first quarter rose 5.1 percent from the end of 1996 to 4.1 billion shekels while assets of the provident funds managed by Hapoalim rose 2.4 percent to 34.3 billion shekels.
A tender is now underway for the sale of a controlling stake of 25 to 70 percent of government-controlled Hapoalim. The tender is due to be completed by the end of August.
